12. Why concave lens is also called diverging lens?
Ans:- A concave lens is called a diverging lens because it spreads out (diverges) the parallel rays of light that fall on it. After
passing through the lens, the rays move away from each other and appear to come from a single point (the principal focus) on
the same side of the lens.
13. Short-sightedness cannot be corrected by the use of a convex lens, why?
Ans:- Short-sightedness cannot be corrected by a convex lens because a convex lens converges light rays, making them meet
even earlier. In short-sightedness, the image already forms in front of the retina, and a convex lens would worsen this by
focusing the light even sooner. Therefore, a concave (diverging) lens is used to move the image back onto the retina.
14. Write two causes of short sightedness.
Ans:- Here are two causes of short-sightedness (myopia):
1. The eyeball becomes too long, causing the image to form in front of the retina.
2. The eye lens becomes too powerful (too convex), bending light more than necessary.
15. What type of defect is found in the given diagram of the eye? Write with reason.
Ans:- In the diagram, the parallel rays of light entering the eye focus in front of the retina instead of
exactly on it. This happens when the eyeball is too long or the eye lens is too powerful, which are
characteristics of myopia.

19. Between glass and water, glass is considered a denser medium and water is a rarer medium. Why?
Ans:- Glass is considered a denser optical medium than water because:
1. Glass refracts light more strongly than water. This means light travels more slowly in glass than in water.
2. The refractive index of glass (about 1.5) is higher than that of water (about 1.33), so glass is optically denser.
Therefore, light bends more when entering glass, making it the denser medium compared to water.
20. When the letters written on the paper are observed from the top of a glass slab the letters appear to be slightly raised.
Why?
Ans:- The letters appear slightly raised when viewed from the top of a glass slab because the light rays coming from the
letters bend away from the normal as they pass from glass to air. Due to this refraction, the letters appear to be at a position
higher than their actual depth.
